limitations: The queued response is independent of the active upstream presence dependency after cache initialization. This is an ordering guarantee, not a numeric startup-latency or provider-performance claim.
Validation uses synthetic employers, postings, clocks and provider gates. It does not measure live-company availability, provider traffic or behavior under production load.
Collection ownership and progress remain local to one server process. Multiple replicas require separate coordination; this change does not introduce shared storage or distributed locking.
The existing browser monitoring deadline includes time spent waiting for presence. A long operation can still require manual reconnection after the ten-minute monitoring limit.

Provider TTLs, manual-refresh minimums, error backoff and posting-body retention policies still determine eligibility. A later catalog request is not guaranteed to avoid provider calls in every state.
The production cache-error reporter is synchronous. Injected async or throwing reporters exercise the service extension boundary and its unexpected-failure contract.
Claude Code reports the requested model identity, but effective backend reasoning effort is not independently exposed. The requested effort is max.
Unanimous agreement is a decision to advance the reviewed stage. It does not establish defect-free behavior or correctness outside the reviewed and executed scope.
